clue.text: Second verse able at last to stir emotions

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
V is the standard abbreviation for verse

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

parts.note: final letter of able

explanation.surface: A poet hopes a second verse will finally stir the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch someone's feelings is a common verb sense, as in a film that brings tears.

clue.text: Human beings in graceless state

parts.note: mortals are humans, as opposed to gods
taken as written

explanation.surface: People are described as living in a fallen condition.
explanation.walkthrough: In Catholic teaching this grave kind of wrongdoing removes sanctifying grace from the soul, which makes 'graceless state' a witty theological definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic doctrine holds such grave wrongdoing cuts the soul off from divine favour until confession.

clue.text: Girl round about inside far from reticent

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the following pieces sit in the middle of the name

parts.note: Val is a short girl's name
O is round in shape
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A girl who was once quiet is now, it seems, anything but.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outspoken who airs opinions loudly is the opposite of reserved or quiet.

clue.text: Speed trap?

parts.note: surface reading: a police radar checkpoint catching fast drivers
setter's reading: trap is slang for mouth, and a speedy one belongs to someone who talks fast and nonstop

explanation.walkthrough: Trap is British slang for the mouth (as in 'shut your trap'), and motor can mean go fast, so the phrase describes a compulsive talker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who chatters endlessly has a mouth that runs at high velocity, a jocular slang term.

clue.text: Headless corpse is sent back for certain journey

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a body is a corpse
is shortened to 's, as in it's

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so its letters are read from right to left

parts.note: yes is the reply meaning definitely, for certain

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a headless body is returned, apparently for a particular trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of Odysseus's wanderings gave its name to any long, eventful voyage.

clue.text: After Ring compose tune in unenclosed space

indicators.note: after says the following words are placed behind the first one in sequence

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to pen is to write or compose
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: After Wagner's Ring cycle, a composer writes a tune for an outdoor concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoors, outside any building or walls, is what this phrase names, as in an outdoor theatre.

clue.text: Scot happened to eat speciality European dish

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word swallows the others

parts.note: Mac is a familiar term for a Scotsman
arose means came about, happened
a niche is a specialised area
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A Scotsman happens to sample a local European delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta baked in a sauce made with cheddar is a familiar comfort food served as a main course.

clue.text: Global peacekeepers against entering unstable Israel

indicators.note: unstable suggests something that will not hold its shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the six letters of Israel rearranged
V is versus, against

explanation.surface: A news story: peacekeepers oppose moving into an unstable Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide applies everywhere and to everyone, the sense of all-embracing.

clue.text: Richmond MP once hot with fever

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an ague is a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A former MP is flushed and feverish.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague was MP for Richmond in North Yorkshire from 1989 to 2015 and once led the Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: William, later Lord, represented that Yorkshire constituency for decades before retiring from parliament.

clue.text: What might be an illicit date?

definitions.text: What might be an illicit date?

parts.words: What might be an illicit date?
parts.note: surface reading: a secret romantic meeting, an affair

parts.words: What might be an illicit date?
parts.note: setter's reading: a date is a fruit from a palm, and one you are not allowed to eat recalls the apple of Eden

explanation.walkthrough: Date means a romantic outing on the surface but is really the fruit; the phrase comes from Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical Eden held a tree whose produce Adam and Eve were told not to eat, now any tempting pleasure.

clue.text: Told to demolish Conservative minister's home

indicators.note: told means spoken to someone, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to wreck is to demolish
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered to knock down a government minister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a church minister, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish clergyman, and his house provided by the church is named after him.

clue.text: Attractive to ignore fine print

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: fetching means attractive
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An attractive contract that tempts you to skip the fine print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine print' looks like one phrase, but fine belongs to the wordplay and print alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An artwork made by biting a design into a metal plate with acid and then inking it onto paper.

clue.text: Improvised excellent book about Donegal's borders

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier words wrap around the next piece

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of Donegal

explanation.surface: An excellent book about the Irish county of Donegal was put together on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken or performed without preparation or a script, made up on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Deep breath?

parts.note: surface reading: a long inhalation to calm yourself
setter's reading: the deep is the ocean, and its breath is the wind blowing off it

explanation.walkthrough: 'The deep' is a poetic name for the ocean, so its breath is a light wind off the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle coastal wind blowing in from the ocean toward land, typically on a warm afternoon.

clue.text: One having loads, rolling in it, after laundering?

definitions.text: One having loads, rolling in it, after laundering?

parts.words: One having loads, rolling in it, after laundering?
parts.note: surface reading: a criminal who has made a fortune and is rich after money laundering

parts.words: One having loads, rolling in it, after laundering?
parts.note: setter's reading: a household appliance takes loads of clothes, which tumble round inside it, once they have been washed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling in it' means very rich, and laundering suggests dirty money; both really describe washing going round in a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic appliance that whirls wet clothes at high speed to remove water after washing.

clue.text: One new coin setter has taken for carrot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
a cent is a coin
the setter says I've, as in I have taken

explanation.surface: A setter admits to taking a fresh coin as a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrot is the reward in 'carrot and stick', not a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangling a reward to motivate someone is the image behind carrot-and-stick persuasion.

clue.text: Makes home given time in monster's loch

indicators.note: given into here means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Loch Ness in Scotland is home of the legendary monster
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Given time, the Loch Ness monster settles in to make its home.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build a little dwelling of twigs, and the verb extends to anyone settling in somewhere cosy.

clue.text: Where to take refuge as truancy treated harshly

indicators.note: something treated harshly is knocked about out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of as and truancy rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil hides somewhere safe because skipping school is punished severely.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy place offering protection, where fugitives traditionally could not be seized.

clue.text: New land area provides iridescent material

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A newly opened plot of land yields a shimmering substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl lines oyster shells and shimmers with rainbow colours when light hits it.

clue.text: Stop intelligence officer infiltrating Kent cricket side?

indicators.note: infiltrating means slipping inside, so these pieces go within the others

parts.note: Kent is a county in the South East of England
MI is Military Intelligence
Col is the abbreviation for colonel
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A spy infiltrates the Kent cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop means a punctuation mark, not halt; the on side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark is called a stop, and this one makes a pause stronger than a comma.

clue.text: FBI agents placed outside division

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: set means placed
G-men is slang for FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: FBI agents are posted outside a department.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece cut or separated from a whole, such as one portion of an orange.

clue.text: Smallest musical note presented with hesitation

parts.note: a minim is a half note
um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A musician hesitates before playing the tiniest note.
explanation.walkthrough: As a definition, the noun means the least possible amount, used adjectivally as in a minimum wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively it describes the lowest permitted or possible quantity, as in minimum wage.

clue.text: Lad from Winchester?

parts.note: surface reading: a boy from the English city or its famous school
setter's reading: Winchester is a make of rifle, so its offspring is the child of a firearm

explanation.walkthrough: Winchester is a city in Hampshire but also a famous American rifle, and the phrase is a jocular term for a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: A jovial exclamation or affectionate term for a scamp, literally the child of a firearm.

clue.text: Where one finds badger and duck in fight

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
a duck is a score of nought in cricket

explanation.surface: A badger and a duck come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief quarrel or scrap, a squabble that breaks out between two people.

clue.text: Holding the French in English court is brilliant success

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so the following pieces surround this one

parts.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
la is French for the

explanation.surface: Detaining a French party in an English court is hailed as a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, it means dazzling effect or conspicuous acclaim for an achievement.

clue.text: Drain to make white, not black

indicators.note: not here means minus, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to bleach is to whiten
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Instructions for whitening something that is no longer dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Water percolating through soil carries away soluble minerals, emptying it of nutrients.

clue.text: Bitter brewed round university gets commendation

indicators.note: brewed means mixed and stirred up, so the letters are reworked
round means surrounding, so the mixed letters wrap the next piece

parts.note: the six letters of bitter rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A pub's bitter, brewed near a university, wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of hoppy pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An act or speech of praise and respect, honouring someone's achievements.

clue.text: Mum garages a small vehicle — will it run?

indicators.note: to garage a car is to put it inside, so the following pieces go within

parts.note: Ma is mother
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Mum puts a little car in the garage and wonders whether it still goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will it run?' sounds like asking whether the car works; really it asks whether eye make-up will smudge when wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelash cosmetic famously streaks down the cheeks when tears or rain wet it, unless waterproof.

clue.text: In AA to meet drunk individually

indicators.note: drunk means staggering and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters of in, AA, to and meet rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning up drunk to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members are encouraged to take things day by day.
explanation.definitionFit: Singly, separately, each in turn rather than together as a group.

clue.text: Carriage bringing husband in for example

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A carriage arrives bringing a husband, to give one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A light horse-drawn two-wheeled vehicle, a dialect form of chaise.
